easy.def: A person who plays the piano.
examples: The pianist played.
She is a pianist.
The pianist took a bow.

more.def: A person who plays the piano.
examples: The pianist played a beautiful song at the concert.
She practiced every day to become a pianist.
The pianist bowed to the cheering audience.

easy.def: A big musical instrument with black and white keys.
examples: I play the piano.
The piano is in the living room.
She sat at the piano.

more.def: A large musical instrument with black and white keys that make sounds when you press them.
examples: She practices the piano for twenty minutes every day.
The piano player pressed the keys softly.
A grand piano filled the center of the stage.

easy.def: To choose one.
examples: Pick a card.
She picked the red one.
I will pick a book.

more.def: To choose one thing or person from a group.
examples: Pick any book from the shelf that you like.
The coach picked her to be team captain.
I picked the biggest pumpkin in the patch.

easy.def: To take fruit or flowers from a plant.
examples: We pick apples.
She picked a flower.
I pick berries.

more.def: To pull fruit, flowers, or leaves off a plant.
examples: We picked strawberries at the farm on Saturday.
She picked a bunch of daisies for her mother.
The farmers pick the apples in the fall.

easy.def: A pointed stick in a fence.
examples: The fence has pickets.
A white picket fence.
The picket is broken.

more.def: A pointed stick or board that stands upright and forms part of a fence.
examples: The white picket fence has pickets that are pointed at the top.
Dad painted each picket of the fence green.
A broken picket let the puppy squeeze out into the yard.

easy.def: A crunchy green snack with a sour taste.
examples: I put a pickle on my burger.
The pickle is sour.
I like pickles.

more.def: A cucumber or other vegetable that has been kept in salty or sour liquid.
examples: I put a pickle on my sandwich.
The pickle was crunchy and sour.
Grandma made pickles from the garden cucumbers.

easy.def: A truck with an open back.
examples: Dad drives a pickup.
The pickup is red.
The pickup carried wood.

more.def: A small truck with an open back for carrying loads.
examples: Dad loaded the hay into the pickup.
The farmer drove a red pickup.
The pickup bumped along the road.

easy.def: Only liking a few things.
examples: He is a picky eater.
A picky cat.
She is picky.

more.def: Hard to please, and only willing to accept certain things, especially in food.
examples: My little brother is a picky eater and will only eat plain pasta.
The cat is so picky that it will not eat anything but one brand of food.
She is picky about which socks she wears.

easy.def: A meal that you eat outside.
examples: We had a picnic in the park.
The picnic is on a blanket.
I like picnics.

more.def: A meal that you pack and eat outdoors, often on a blanket.
examples: We had a picnic by the lake.
Mom packed sandwiches for the picnic.
The rain ruined our picnic.

easy.def: A drawing, a painting or a photo.
examples: I drew a picture of my dog.
There is a picture on the wall.
Mom took a picture of us.

more.def: A drawing, painting or photograph that shows how something looks.
examples: She painted a picture of the mountains.
Dad took a picture of us at the beach.
A picture of a dragon is on the book's cover.

easy.def: To see something in your mind.
examples: Picture a big red balloon.
I can picture my house.
Can you picture the beach?

more.def: To form an image of something in your mind.
examples: Close your eyes and picture a quiet forest.
He pictured himself winning the race.
I can picture the whole room, with the red couch.

easy.def: A baked treat with a crust and filling.
examples: I ate apple pie.
We bake a pie.
The pie is hot.

more.def: A baked food with a pastry crust and a sweet or salty filling.
examples: Grandma baked an apple pie.
We had pumpkin pie after dinner.
The pie cooled on the windowsill.

easy.def: A part of something bigger.
examples: I ate a piece of pie.
A piece fell off the toy.
Give me a piece of paper.

more.def: A part that has been cut, broken or taken from a whole thing.
examples: She cut the cake into twelve equal pieces.
One piece of the puzzle was missing.
He tore a piece of tape off the roll.

easy.def: One work of music, writing or art.
examples: She played a piece on the piano.
That piece of music is slow.
The art show has a piece by every child.

more.def: A single work of music, writing or art.
examples: The orchestra played a lovely piece by a famous composer.
The student read a short piece of her writing to the class.
He painted a piece for the school gallery.

easy.def: A platform that sticks out into the water.
examples: We fished off the pier.
The pier is long.
Boats tie up at the pier.

more.def: A long platform that stretches from the shore out over water, where boats can stop.
examples: We fished off the end of the pier.
The pier stuck out into the sea.
The ferry docked at the pier.

easy.def: A farm animal with a curly tail.
examples: The pig rolled in mud.
Pigs oink.
A pig lives on the farm.

more.def: A farm animal with a round body, short legs, a curly tail and a flat nose.
examples: The pig rolled in the mud to keep cool.
Farmers raise pigs for food.
A pig can run faster than you might think.

easy.def: A gray bird that lives in cities.
examples: A pigeon sat on the roof.
The pigeon eats crumbs.
Pigeons coo.

more.def: A plump bird with gray feathers that is often seen in cities and parks.
examples: A pigeon pecked at the crumbs in the park.
Pigeons nest on the ledges of tall buildings.
The pigeon cooed softly on the roof.

easy.def: A little pig.
examples: The piggy rolled in the mud.
I saw a piggy on the farm.
A piggy oinked at me.

more.def: A pig, especially a small or young one.
examples: A little piggy rolled in the mud on the farm.
Every piggy in the pen wanted a turn at the trough.
The children laughed as the piggy chased the farmer for food.

easy.def: A baby pig.
examples: The piglet is pink.
A piglet squealed.
We saw a piglet on the farm.

more.def: A baby pig, usually one that is still drinking its mother's milk.
examples: The little piglet squealed as it ran after its mother.
A sow can have ten piglets at one time.
The farmer fed a hungry piglet from a bottle.

easy.def: A lot of things on top of each other.
examples: I made a pile of leaves.
A pile of books is on the desk.
The pile of laundry is big.

more.def: A group of things lying one on top of another.
examples: The kids jumped into a pile of leaves.
A pile of books sat on the desk.
She put the dirty clothes in a pile.

easy.def: To put things on top of each other.
examples: Pile the books on the table.
She piled the toys.
Snow piled up.

more.def: To make a heap of things.
examples: He piled the wood next to the fireplace.
Snow piled up against the door.
She piled all the cushions on the floor.

easy.def: A traveler on a religious trip.
examples: The pilgrim walked to the shrine.
Pilgrims traveled far.
The pilgrim carried a staff.

more.def: A person who travels to a holy place for religious reasons.
examples: The pilgrim walked many miles to the shrine.
Pilgrims traveled far to the holy city.
The Pilgrims sailed to America on a ship.

easy.def: A small tablet of medicine.
examples: He took a pill.
The pill is small.
Swallow the pill with water.

more.def: A small, hard piece of medicine that you swallow.
examples: He took a pill with a glass of water.
The pill helped stop her headache.
The doctor gave me a pill for my cough.

easy.def: A tall, strong post that holds up a building.
examples: A pillar holds up the roof.
The building has tall pillars.
I stood by the pillar.

more.def: A tall, strong post made of stone, brick or metal that holds up part of a building or stands as a monument.
examples: Stone pillars held up the roof of the ancient temple.
A tall pillar stood in the middle of the square.
The bridge rests on thick pillars sunk deep in the river.

easy.def: A soft cushion for your head in bed.
examples: I sleep on a pillow.
The pillow is soft.
I hugged my pillow.

more.def: A soft bag filled with feathers or foam that you rest your head on.
examples: I put my head on a soft pillow.
The kids had a pillow fight.
She hugged her pillow and fell asleep.

easy.def: A person who flies a plane.
examples: The pilot flew the plane.
My uncle is a pilot.
The pilot said hello.

more.def: A person who flies an airplane or other aircraft.
examples: The pilot announced the weather.
My uncle is a pilot for an airline.
The pilot landed the plane safely.

easy.def: A small red bump on the skin.
examples: I have a pimple on my chin.
A pimple is tiny.
She had a pimple on her nose.

more.def: A small, red, sore bump on the skin, which many teenagers get.
examples: He had a pimple on his chin the morning of the photo.
Washing your face can help with a pimple.
The doctor said the small pimple would go away by itself.

easy.def: A thin, short piece of metal with a sharp point.
examples: Mom used a pin to hold the cloth.
I found a pin on the floor.
Put a pin in the map.

more.def: A small, thin piece of metal with a sharp point, used to hold things together.
examples: The tailor held the cloth with a pin.
She put a pin in the map to show where we went.
A pin on the corkboard held up the notice.

easy.def: To stick something on a wall.
examples: She pinned the paper to the board.
I pin my name tag on.
Pin the card to the wall.

more.def: To fasten something in place using a small, sharp piece of metal.
examples: The teacher pinned our drawings to the board.
He pinned a ribbon on his shirt.
Mom pinned up the hem of my pants.

easy.def: To squeeze something between your finger and thumb.
examples: I pinch my nose.
She pinched the dough.
The crab pinched me.

more.def: To press something tightly between your thumb and finger.
examples: I pinched my nose at the smell.
She pinched the edges of the pie crust.
The crab pinched my finger.

easy.def: A very small amount.
examples: Add a pinch of salt.
I put in a pinch.
A pinch of sugar.

more.def: A very small amount of something that you can hold between your finger and thumb.
examples: Add a pinch of salt to the soup.
She sprinkled a pinch of sugar on top.
The recipe calls for a pinch of pepper.

easy.def: A tall tree with needles that stays green.
examples: The pine tree is tall.
Pine cones fall.
We cut a pine tree.

more.def: A tall evergreen tree with long, thin needles and cones.
examples: The pine tree stayed green all winter.
Pine needles covered the ground.
We hiked through a forest of pines.

easy.def: A sweet yellow fruit with a prickly skin.
examples: I ate a pineapple.
The pineapple is sweet.
We put pineapple on the pizza.

more.def: A large, sweet, juicy tropical fruit with a rough, spiky skin and leaves at the top.
examples: The pineapple has a rough, spiky skin, but the inside is sweet and juicy.
We cut the pineapple into slices for the picnic.
Pineapples grow in warm places such as Hawaii.

easy.def: The hard, scaly seed case of a pine tree.
examples: I found a pinecone.
The pinecone is brown.
We collected pinecones.

more.def: The hard, brown, scaly case that holds the seeds of a pine tree.
examples: I found a big pinecone under the tree and took it home.
A pinecone opens when it is dry and closes when it is wet.
We painted pinecones to make holiday decorations.

easy.def: A short, high sound like a small bell or a message alert.
examples: I heard a ping.
My phone made a ping.
The ping was loud.

more.def: A short, high, ringing sound, such as the sound of a small bell or a message arriving.
examples: I heard a ping when a message came in.
A ping told us the oven was ready.
The ping of the bell echoed in the room.

easy.def: To make a short, high ringing sound.
examples: My phone pings.
The oven pinged.
The bell pinged.

more.def: To make a short, high ringing sound, or to send a quick message to someone.
examples: My phone pings when I get a message.
The oven pinged when the cake was ready.
A bell pinged softly in the hallway.

easy.def: Light red.
examples: The flower is pink.
She wears a pink dress.
A pink balloon.

more.def: Having a light red color, like cotton candy.
examples: The sunset turned the sky pink.
She wore a pink ribbon in her hair.
The pink flowers bloomed in spring.

easy.def: The color light red.
examples: Pink is my favorite color.
Mix red and white for pink.
The walls are painted pink.

more.def: A light red color made by mixing red and white.
examples: Mix red and white to make pink.
The sky glowed in shades of pink.
Pink is a soft color.

easy.def: The smallest finger.
examples: I hurt my pinkie.
She crossed her pinkies.
My pinkie is small.

more.def: The smallest finger on the hand.
examples: I hurt my pinkie when I closed the door on it.
We made a pinkie promise.
She held the teacup with her pinkie out.

easy.def: To find the exact place or cause of something.
examples: I pinpointed the spot on the map.
We pinpointed the leak.
She pinpointed the problem.

more.def: To find or show exactly where something is or what the cause is.
examples: I pinpointed our town on the map with a small tack.
The mechanic pinpointed the cause of the noise.
The scientists pinpointed the exact spot where the meteor landed.

easy.def: A small amount of liquid, about two cups.
examples: We bought a pint of milk.
A pint of berries is small.
He drank a pint of water.

more.def: A measure of liquid equal to two cups, or half a quart.
examples: The recipe calls for a pint of cream.
We bought a pint of strawberries at the market.
Two pints make one quart.

easy.def: A person who goes first to a new place and makes a home there.
examples: The pioneers moved west.
A pioneer built a cabin.
Pioneers worked hard.

more.def: A person who is one of the first to explore or live in a new place.
examples: The pioneers traveled west in covered wagons.
A pioneer built a log cabin by the river.
Pioneers worked hard to build homes in the wild land.

easy.def: A person who is first to try something new.
examples: She is a pioneer in science.
He is a pioneer of flight.
A pioneer of music.

more.def: A person who is among the first to try a new idea or way of doing something.
examples: She is a pioneer in science and has made new discoveries.
The Wright brothers were pioneers of flight.
He was a pioneer of music for children.

easy.def: A tube that water or gas moves through.
examples: Water runs through the pipe.
The pipe is leaking.
A pipe is under the sink.

more.def: A long, hollow tube that carries water, gas or other things from one place to another.
examples: The plumber fixed the broken pipe under the sink.
Pipes bring clean water to every house in town.
A frozen pipe burst in the cold winter.

easy.def: A long pipe that carries water, oil or gas.
examples: The pipeline is long.
A pipeline carries oil.
The pipeline crosses the desert.

more.def: A long line of pipes that carries water, oil or gas from one place to another.
examples: A long pipeline carries oil across the desert to the coast.
The new water pipeline brings fresh water to the city.
Workers buried the pipeline underground.

easy.def: A robber who sails the sea in a ship.
examples: The pirate had a patch on his eye.
Pirates hide treasure.
I dressed as a pirate.

more.def: A person who sails on the sea and steals from other ships, in stories and in the past.
examples: The pirate buried his treasure on the island.
Pirates sailed the seas in tall ships.
The pirate in the story had a parrot on his shoulder.

easy.def: A small green nut in a hard shell.
examples: I ate a pistachio.
Pistachios are green.
We cracked the pistachios.

more.def: A small, green nut with a thin, hard shell that is eaten as a snack or used to flavor ice cream.
examples: We cracked pistachios and ate the green nuts inside.
Pistachio ice cream is pale green.
The pistachio shell splits open when it is ripe.

easy.def: A part in an engine that moves up and down.
examples: A piston moves up and down.
The engine has pistons.
The piston is metal.

more.def: A part inside an engine that moves up and down inside a tube and makes other parts move.
examples: Each piston moves up and down inside a tube in the engine.
The mechanic replaced a worn piston in the car's engine.
A piston pushes the liquid out of the pump.

easy.def: A big hole in the ground.
examples: We dug a pit.
The pit is deep.
They fell into the pit.

more.def: A large hole in the ground.
examples: We dug a pit for the campfire.
The workers dug a deep pit.
A cat fell into the muddy pit.

easy.def: The hard seed in a fruit like a peach.
examples: I spit out the pit.
The cherry has a pit.
The peach pit is hard.

more.def: The large, hard seed in the middle of some fruits, such as a peach or cherry.
examples: Be careful, there is a pit in the cherry.
He planted a peach pit in the garden.
The olive has a small pit.

easy.def: To throw a ball to the batter.
examples: He will pitch the ball.
The pitcher pitched fast.
She pitched the ball.

more.def: To throw the ball in baseball toward the batter.
examples: He pitched the ball right over the plate.
The coach pitched to each player during practice.
She pitched all nine innings.

easy.def: To set up a tent.
examples: We pitch the tent.
They pitched camp by the lake.
Dad pitched our tent.

more.def: To put up a tent and fix it in place.
examples: We pitched our tent beside the river.
They pitched camp at the edge of the woods.
Dad pitched the tent before it got dark.

easy.def: How high or low a sound is.
examples: The bird sang at a high pitch.
Her voice has a low pitch.
The pitch of the note went up.

more.def: How high or low a musical note or sound is.
examples: A violin plays a high pitch, and a tuba a low one.
The pitch of her voice rose when she got excited.
The tuner checks the pitch of each piano string.

easy.def: The baseball player who throws the ball to the batter.
examples: The pitcher threw the ball.
He is the pitcher.
The pitcher is fast.

more.def: The baseball player who throws the ball for the batter to hit.
examples: The pitcher threw a fast ball over the plate.
He is the best pitcher on our team.
The pitcher wound up and threw a curve.

easy.def: A tall container for pouring liquids.
examples: The pitcher is full of juice.
Pour from the pitcher.
Mom filled the pitcher.

more.def: A container with a handle and a lip for pouring drinks.
examples: The pitcher is full of cold lemonade.
Mom filled the pitcher with water.
She poured juice from the pitcher into everyone's cup.

easy.def: So sad that you feel sorry for it.
examples: The kitten gave a pitiful cry.
The pitiful puppy was wet.
It looked pitiful.

more.def: Very sad, in a way that makes you feel sorry.
examples: The kitten gave a pitiful cry from the rainy yard.
The pitiful puppy shivered in the cold.
The garden looked pitiful after the long dry spell.

easy.def: A sad feeling for someone who is having a hard time.
examples: I felt pity for the lost puppy.
She felt pity for him.
The story filled me with pity.

more.def: A feeling of sorrow for someone who is in trouble or pain.
examples: He felt pity for the lost kitten shivering in the rain.
She looked at the old man with pity.
The children showed pity for the hurt bird.

easy.def: Something that makes you sad or sorry.
examples: It is a pity you cannot come.
What a pity it rained!
It's a pity the game ended.

more.def: A cause for sadness or disappointment.
examples: It is a pity that you missed the show.
What a pity the picnic was canceled.
It would be a pity to waste this good food.

easy.def: A round, flat bread with cheese and tomato.
examples: I love pizza.
We ate pizza for dinner.
The pizza is hot.

more.def: A flat, round bread baked with tomato sauce, cheese and other toppings.
examples: We ordered a pizza with cheese.
Pizza is baked in a hot oven.
She added mushrooms to her pizza.
